Design for the user's primary decision; make the relevant comparisons visible together. (DR-006)
Give quantitative claims appropriate units, periods, baselines, and denominators. A context selector passing does not prove the data is correct. (DR-003)
Prefer aligned tables, small multiples, and nearby explanations when they reduce comparison effort. (DR-006)
Use space for useful information; justify oversized headers, nested cards, and repeated decorative labels. (DR-008)
Calibrate density to the page's task and viewport. Preserve readable type, interaction affordances, and useful whitespace; do not maximize a density score. (DR-006, DR-007)
Keep chart scales, missing values, and uncertainty honest. Review these visually and against chart configuration; DOM geometry cannot establish graphical integrity. (DR-001, DR-002, DR-004, DR-005)
Treat these as Tufte-inspired design guidance, not quotations or universal layout requirements. Honor project design systems and explicit user feedback.
Keep controls usable as density increases; start with at least 24 by 24 CSS px for ordinary controls and review actual target geometry and exceptions. (DR-007)
Use bounded reading widths and natural word spacing for prose. Avoid fully justified paragraphs; adapt reading measure to the language and task. (DR-007)
Align numeric amounts and headers consistently; use suitable precision and tabular digits to support scanning. Distinguish identifiers from amounts. (DR-006)

Keep each component's identifying graphic, title, and description associated. Measure their relative placement and require visuals per item; a parent grid declaration or one visible icon cannot establish the whole list is correct. (DR-006, DR-008)
Reduce redundant spacing before reducing readable type. Let wrapping and enlarged text determine item height; keep exact icon sizes, gaps, and column choices in the project contract. (DR-007)
Carry an entity's visual identity from discovery to detail. Compare the actual graphic as well as its stable identity; matching symbol labels alone do not establish matching artwork. (DR-005)
Declare visual peers and their intended anchors. Align comparable headings, labels, controls, and component edges; preserve purposeful indentation and optical exceptions. (DR-017)
Use consistent gaps for equivalent relationships and clearer separation between unrelated groups. Scope wrapped content separately; preserve text adaptation and usable controls. (DR-018)

Allocate space to task value, not container availability. Compare distinct visible evidence across viewports, cap only explicitly declared chrome, and preserve whitespace when a finite task is complete. (DR-019)

Give semantic peers deliberate comparable treatment while allowing asymmetry for unequal priorities. Footprint ratios are geometry proxies, not attention scores; never force equal heights by hiding content. (DR-020)
